questions.text: My body seems to store emotional charge that I can feel building over the course of a stressful week.
I prioritize long-term wellbeing over short-term pleasure when the two conflict.
When I understand why someone is suffering, I still rarely want their situation to change.
I find it hard to tell when someone is genuinely asking for my opinion versus looking for validation.
I see my job as walking the path alongside the group, wherever it leads.
I detect when someone uses vague language like 'some people think' to express their own opinion without owning it.
I maintain an archive of past work so I can reference and build on it.
My emotional system operates with a kind of quiet competence that I've come to trust.
I routinely visualize my own future success and make decisions to bring that vision closer.
I feel most fulfilled when I have given away more than I have kept.
When I think again about a hardship someone faces, I still want them to find relief.
I view deferring to others as a service to the group.
I find it hard to tell when someone is being sarcastic versus sincere.
Others' suffering matters to me whatever mood I am in.
I often have multiple projects going at once and move between them as my interest dictates.
I sense when the real decision-maker in a meeting is not the person with the highest title.
I compare my current progress to my original timeline to gauge whether I'm ahead or behind.
Hearing that someone has been badly hurt leaves me wanting to reach out to them.
I focus on the explicit agenda of a meeting rather than the interpersonal dynamics.
Even when I know I could easily help someone in pain, I feel little wish to.
I tend to ask for the raise, the upgrade, or the better deal without hesitation.
Someone's ongoing hardship rarely stays on my mind once I am no longer with them.
My body is always the first to tell me how I'm feeling, often before I have words for it.
I focus on the conversation during meetings and trust the key points will stick.
I would give up a cherished personal goal if doing so served a greater collective need.
I tend to donate or share resources before setting aside savings for myself.
When I'm in a beautiful place, the experience can feel almost painfully vivid.
I feel a strong pull to shape the agenda of any group I am part of.
My emotional spectrum is real and present but it operates in pastel tones rather than neon.
I negotiate and make requests without scripted fallbacks, adapting to the flow of conversation.
I prefer that ground rules emerge from group discussion before activity begins.
I experience the anticipation before a big moment as a mild heightening of attention, not a surge of adrenaline.
I tend to make executive decisions about scope changes mid-project.
I detect when someone is subtly seeking validation in the way they tell a story.
I feel that taking a solo trip to recharge is more valuable than a group vacation.
I enjoy being the public face of a group effort.
